title: Verify the Claude Code plugin in a real session with --plugin-dir
body:
Start a resident first (node src/cli.js ui as a background task) and wait until GET /api/resident reports retrieval semantic. Then, in a scratch git project, run claude -p "<prompt>" --plugin-dir <checkout> --allowedTools Bash --output-format stream-json --verbose < /dev/null and read hook_response events and assistant text from the JSONL. Read recorded observations from ~/.claude/plugins/data/dd-inline/<project-key>/index.sqlite (table memory_observations), and delete that directory afterwards (stop the resident first; it holds the file open).

Why: --plugin-dir loads hooks/hooks.json exactly as the marketplace install does, for that run only. A resident that a hook starts inside a Bash tool call dies when the call ends, and while it loads DD is inactive: session start then omits the retrieve/propose guidance and project context, so a probe without a ready resident looks like a regression. Text output mode shows only the reply to the Stop reminder, hiding the rest.

evidence.summary: An inactive resident returns only the banner and residentNotice; PULL_GUIDANCE and advisory context are added only when active.
Plugin hooks anchored at ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, including PostToolUseFailure.
Anchored delivery: keywords validated against this memory's own text and a generic-request corpus before proposing.

v1.trigger: When a change to hooks, session start or capture must be confirmed in a real Claude Code session, without installing the plugin into the user's global config
